title: audit plugin per-repo config (.claude/audit.config.json)
description: Layer 1 of the plugin's extensibility model. Every key is optional; omitted keys fall back to the defaults in hooks/_config.py DEFAULTS. Unknown keys are tolerated (forward-compat) but reported as warnings by validate-config.py.

default.description: The verdict for anything no rule matches. Default 'allow'. Set 'deny' for the deny-all-then-permit shape, and list what you permit in `allow`.

allow.description: Name patterns that are permitted. Has no effect while `default` is 'allow' - everything not denied is already allowed.

deny.description: Name patterns that are refused. Deny beats allow. A pattern matching one of audit's own commands/skills/agents does not take effect and is reported as a finding rather than silently ignored.

areas.description: Rules scoped to a `meta.areas` tag, in force only while a phase tagged with it has work in_progress. Any active area's `deny` wins; several active areas UNION their `allow` lists (documented fail-open).

manifestPath.description: Path (project-dir-relative) to the audit manifest JSON. Default docs/audit/audit-plan.json.

gitRoot.description: Path (project-dir-relative) of the git repository root where git + build/gate commands run. Default '.'.

exemptGlobs.description: Globs whose edits skip the plan-first / TDD / bash-write guards (docs, tests, .claude/**, the manifest).

enforce.description: LEGACY: force the plan-first gate to DENY regardless of evidence — planGate: "deny" says the same thing, and planGate wins when both are set. Default false, which grades the gate: observe with no manifest, warn with a manifest but no phase in_progress, deny once a phase is running. What is graded is the plan-coverage class wherever it is enforced: require-plan's Edit/Write path, the shell-write branch of guard-secrets-read and the PostToolUse report in guard-bash-writes all resolve the same tier. The secret guards are never graded and deny at every tier.

planGate.description: Pin the plan-first gate to one tier by hand instead of grading it on evidence: observe (record only, report once per session), warn (advisory), ask (each out-of-plan edit waits for the human's approval — approving covers one edit), deny (refuse). Absent (the default) the gate grades itself: observe with no manifest, warn with a manifest but nothing running, deny once a phase is in_progress. Beats the legacy enforce when both are set; a value outside the enum is read as unset (fail-open, never deny) and flagged by validate-config.py. Reaches every plan-coverage surface, not just require-plan's Edit path: the shell-write branch of guard-secrets-read and the PostToolUse report in guard-bash-writes resolve the same tier, so one file gets one verdict whichever way it is written. The secret guards are never graded and deny at every tier.

trivialLineThreshold.description: First-touch file edits at or below this many lines are allowed without a plan. Default 80.

stateDir.description: Directory for the hooks' transactional state files. Default .claude/state.

bypassKeyword.description: Single-use keyword in a prompt that arms a plan-first bypass for the next edit. Default #no-plan.

secretPatterns.description: Secret-file detection tuning for the read guard.

extra.description: Extra regexes matched against a path to treat it as a secret file.

tokenVars.description: Identifier names that must never be logged (console.log/print of these is blocked).

customRules.description: Opt-in per-path banned patterns. Each rule blocks bannedPattern when pathPrefix appears ANYWHERE in the edited path - it is a substring test, not a prefix test, despite the key's name.

pathPrefix.description: Substring the rule applies under: it fires when this text occurs anywhere in the path the edit tool reported (usually absolute), so 'realtime/' matches src/realtime/x.ts as well as libs/realtime/y.ts. The key is named pathPrefix for compatibility with configs already in the field; the match has always been a substring one.

bannedPattern.description: Regex that, if present in the new content, blocks the edit.

message.description: Explanation shown when the rule fires.

bashWriteCheck.description: Post-Bash unplanned-source-write detector. This is the master off switch and not the only key that decides whether its plan-coverage class speaks: with it enabled, that class still resolves a tier through the plan gate, so planGate: "observe" — or simply a repo with no manifest — silences it. The lock and journal classes bind their claim to evidence of their own and report at every tier.

enabled.description: Enable the git-status diff after Bash. Default true; see the parent description for the tier the plan-coverage class still has to clear.

sourceGlobs.description: Globs that count as source (warn candidates).

testGlobs.description: Globs that count as tests (touching one silences the nudge).

throttleMinutes.description: Per-session minimum gap between warnings. Default 10.

inProgressPolicy.description: Interplay with in_progress audit tasks. 'skip-gate-only' (default) or 'skip-all'. "warn-always" ignores manifest coverage entirely.

usage.description: Token metering (meter-usage.py, /audit:usage). The ledger records counts, model ids, timestamps, branch and author - never prompt content.

ledgerDir.description: Repo-relative directory holding the monthly NDJSON ledger and its scan cursors. Default '.claude/usage'. Deliberately outside stateDir, which is GC'd after 7 days.

authorMode.description: How the spender is recorded: git user.email (default), git user.name, a short salt-free sha256 ('hash', pseudonymous but still groupable), or no author at all.

showCost.description: Show equivalent API cost alongside tokens. Default true. Labelled 'equiv' because subscription plans carry no per-token bill.

backfillOnFirstRun.description: On first sight of a transcript, scan it from the start (bounded by maxScanBytes) instead of metering only from now on. Default true.

maxScanBytes.description: First-sight backfill ceiling in bytes; above it the scan seeks to EOF so the 10s hook timeout stays safe. Default 33554432 (32 MiB). '/audit:usage --backfill' has no ceiling.

currency.description: Currency label for the pricing table. Default 'USD'.

pricingAsOf.description: Date the shipped pricing table was accurate, surfaced in the report so a stale rate is visible.

bands.description: Absolute cost thresholds that sort tasks into typical / high / outlier. Both null (the default) means the bands calibrate from this project's own completed tasks (median/p90), which needs no guess to mean something on day one. Set BOTH to band by a real budget instead - highUSD must be > 0 and <= outlierUSD, and a pair that isn't falls back to the relative basis rather than classifying anything wrongly. NOT named 'risk': tasks already carry a `risk` field, meaning risk of the change.

highUSD.description: Equivalent USD above which one task's spend counts as high.

outlierUSD.description: Equivalent USD above which one task's spend counts as an outlier.

pricing.description: Model id -> rate row. Lookup is exact match, then longest matching prefix (so a dated id resolves to its family), then the '_default' row.

additionalProperties.description: USD per MILLION tokens for one model. Cache rates follow the published multipliers off base input: write 1.25x at the 5-minute TTL, 2x at the 1-hour TTL, read 0.1x.

policy.description: Which skills, subagents and MCP tools may be used in this project (hooks/guard-capabilities.py + scripts/governance/_policy.py). Shipped INERT: every kind defaults to 'allow' with empty lists, which cannot refuse anything, so a repo that writes nothing behaves as it did before 0.30.0. Resolution order: audit's own commands/skills/agents are always allowed -> a `deny` match (project-wide, or in any area with work in progress) -> an `allow` match (several active areas UNION their allow lists) -> `default`. Patterns are case-sensitive fnmatch globs against the name the tool call uses: the Skill tool's `skill`, the Task/Agent tool's `subagent_type`, or the whole MCP tool name (so 'mcp__github__*' names a server). Governs the tool, not the knowledge; only while the plugin is enabled; may be advisory inside a subagent (anthropics/claude-code#43772 - /audit:doctor warns when the hook has never fired). See SECURITY.md.

enabled.description: Enforce the policy. Default true - which changes nothing on its own, since the shipped block allows everything.

onViolation.description: What a violation does: 'deny' (default) refuses the tool call, 'ask' prompts for manual approval per call, 'warn' lets it through with a message. 'warn' is deliberately not a permissionDecision - an advisory must not grant anything.

skills.description: Rules matched against the Skill tool's `skill` argument, e.g. 'dataviz' or 'audit:next'.

agents.description: Rules matched against the Task/Agent tool's `subagent_type`. A call that names none is the general-purpose agent, and is matched as 'general-purpose'.

mcp.description: Rules matched against the whole MCP tool name, e.g. 'mcp__github__get_issue'; 'mcp__github__*' is how a whole server is named.

journal.description: The tamper-evident audit trail (scripts/governance/audit-journal.py + hooks/journal-writes.py): an append-only, hash-chained record of every edit-tool write to the manifest and to this config. Tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof - editing, deleting or reordering a row breaks the chain and `audit-journal.py verify` names it, but with no secret key a forger who rewrites the whole file produces a chain that verifies. See SECURITY.md.

enabled.description: Record manifest and config writes. Default true.

dir.description: Where the monthly per-writer .jsonl files live, relative to the project dir. null (the default) keeps the journal beside the manifest, so it is committed by the same commit that carries the change it records.

strictManifestState.description: Opt-in confirmation prompt (guard-edits.py) when an edit changes manifest STATE - a task or phase's status, completedAt, commit or attempts. 'ask' surfaces the tool call for approval; 'off' (the default) leaves detection to the journal and the doctor. There is deliberately no 'deny': the orchestrator completes tasks through the same edit tools.

ui.description: The look of the panel and the report (scripts/_ui_theme.py). No hook reads this - it is published here because this file is where the config's shape is stated, and a key the validator knows and the schema does not is how the two drifted before.

theme.description: A shipped preset NAME ('slate-teal') or a path to a theme file, absolute or relative to the project dir. null (the default) means SEARCH: .claude/audit.theme.json in the project, then ~/.claude/audit.theme.json, then the built-in preset - and every surface says which of the four it is wearing. A path that is not a file is reported rather than silently ignored, because a theme that quietly did nothing sends its author looking for the bug in the wrong place.

priority.description: Phase prioritisation (scripts/manifest/_priority.py): which phase the orchestrator reaches for first among the work that is ALREADY ready. Nothing here changes readiness - a dependency always wins.

maxTier.description: The highest tier the panel's control offers and the CLI suggests. ADVISORY, AND NOTHING IS CLAMPED: a phase pinned above it keeps the tier it was given and sorts after every tier at or under the maximum by ordinary arithmetic, and the surfaces say so. A clamped value would be a file that says one thing and a run that does another. Default 9.
